chapter: New York, the Kentucky Club and the high-hat
title: Designing drums for the Leedy factory
summary: A company executive hires Greer as drum designer; five trunks of gleaming drums arrive and impress the gangsters.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: How did you get to start designing the drums?

That's when I started. A fellow, one of the executives of the club come to New York and seen me playing at the Kentucky Club. He said, 'Sonny, how would you like to work for us?' I said, 'What doing?' He said, 'designing, and using all our advance products.' I said, 'all right.' I say, 'well, send me a set.' Well, they sent me five trunks of drums. Vibraphones, everything. The picture's up there on the wall. So I come in the

had that stuff! Cotton Club. Ain't no drummer Nothing! They still ain't got it! All this stuff come, five trunks of it. I sit on the bandstand and they sparkle like -- and man when them gangsters saw that, they say, My God, and when a guy want to get a job in a cabaret, the man say 'You got drums like Sonny,' and the guy say, 'You must be crazy, that drum set cost me $3,000 -- didn't cost me nothing, they sent it, but they don't know that.
Now, I'm going to sit behind $3,000.00 worth of drums. I didn't have to play them. All I had to do was look pretty. Get Jo Jones to tell you some time.
